packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING — packet 10

Only supplied neutral prompt, packet metadata and images consulted. No proposed work/author or earlier reading exposed.

Layout
Two upright photographs of a broad cut fragment. Four vertical writing zones are visible across each face, the outermost ones truncated by the cut edges. The large central blank strip suggests two facing page areas, each originally with two columns, but that reconstruction is tentative. The text begins in mid-line at the upper cut and ends above a broad lower blank margin. Brown/gray small cursive text alternates with much larger, darker formal words introducing sections. No colored rubric, running title, or clear marginal gloss is visible. Tiny marks occur in the central blank area of image-002; their function is uncertain. No consistent underlining is apparent. Mirrored holes suggest opposite sides of the same fragment; these are not repeated crops of one text surface.

Selection
I selected the conspicuous formal opening in image-001's far-right zone and an enlarged argument opening in image-002's center-right zone. Surrounding cursive prose was inspected, but it is too abbreviated and faint for me to recover two continuous passages responsibly. The following is a limited record of what I can distinguish.

Numbering: zones A–D run left to right. Text baselines are counted from each zone's first visible line, including top-edge fragments. Counts marked ? are approximate because the cut upper lines cannot always be separated; original y coordinates also locate each sample.

Sample A — image-001.jpg zone D:
image-001.jpg D5? (y≈380): Individuū ē q[cut at right]
image-001.jpg D6? (y≈470): [illegible] p̄ [illegible] mortalis? [illegible; cut at right]
image-001.jpg D7? (y≈530): [illegible]
image-001.jpg D8? (y≈600): [illegible]
image-001.jpg D9? (y≈660): [illegible]
image-001.jpg D10? (y≈720): [illegible]
image-001.jpg D11? (y≈785): [illegible]
image-001.jpg D12? (y≈845): Arguitur? [illegible; cut at right]

The enlarged first word is substantially clearer than its following text. ē could be expanded (est); I have not supplied the cut word after q. The cursive lines are not asserted to be a separate commentary on that opening.

Sample B — image-002.jpg zone C:
image-002.jpg C9? (y≈705): Arguitur Virtus?
image-002.jpg C10? (y≈760): [illegible] p̄ [illegible]
image-002.jpg C11? (y≈820): [illegible]

image-002.jpg C14? (y≈1000): [illegible]

Additional formal transition inspected, not a third passage:
image-001.jpg C20? (y≈1040): Arguitur [illegible]
A further large word lower in image-002 zone C appears to be Replicat̄?; not transcribed as secure text.

No confident deletion or interlinear addition identified. Apparent darker strokes may simply be the enlarged textual hand, rather than correction.

Transforms
Full images surveyed. image-001 dimensions 2837×2493; image-002 2838×2566. Native unfiltered crops: image-001 (1418,922)–(2127,1421); image-002 (1731,564)–(2412,1103); image-001 (2120,270)–(2650,920). No rotation, resampling, contrast modification or reconstruction. Crops overlap the complete images and do not represent extra lines.

Limitations
Most small writing remains unread, including all connecting prose needed for a reliable long source match. Cuts remove original beginnings and ends, and line counts are consequently approximate. A specialist second reading and sharper original photography may help; a wider photograph cannot recover material physically absent from this fragment. Do not expand the above fragments into an assumed philosophical formulation.
